candidate: Centaur-style hybrid search (classical optimizer holds state, LLM proposes a minority of trials); arXiv 2603.24647 v5

cheap_local_trial: WSL2, existing Optuna helper: 20 trials of 30 seconds on a tiny character-level language model, TPE alone against TPE plus one agent-enqueued trial in four, 3 seeds each; about 60 minutes

candidate: Executable finite-state loop controller enforced by hooks (arXiv 2611.10884 v1)
what: Workflow state lives on disk outside the model context; a pre-tool hook checks each tool call against the current state, transitions pass hard shell checks, and a stop hook refuses to end the turn outside declared pause points
problem_here: The unattended loop (hypothesis, change, run, keep or revert) must not drift: skipped steps, batched steps and early stopping are the measured failure modes of prompt-only procedures
mechanism: Per-agent state stack kept by a process outside the agent; PreToolUse gate on permissions per state; transition guards with atomic commit; Stop gate; optional second-model review of a transition
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.10884v1 (2026-11-07), pre-registered, measured by the authors: compliance 27.8% with reminders against 94.8% with the state machine on a small model (8 seeds, +90.9 of 200 items, 95% CI 46.2 to 130.2); stop gate alone scored 5.7 against 76.3 for reminders; 10.64 against 3.01 US dollars per session; gain positive in 1 of 3 seeds on a larger model; lost on one domain from over-strict checks
maturity: Paper v1 2026-11-07, CC BY-NC-ND, no code released; one procedure task plus two secondary benchmarks; no replication
cost: 3.5 to 11 times agent spend in the paper; over-strict guards block valid work; static permissions do not bind an action to the current item; needs both a pre-tool hook and a stop hook on every supported agent product
simpler_alternative: Extend the existing guard hook to read one loop-state file written by expctl, with transition checks inside expctl and no daemon or second model
reason: Strongest measured remedy for procedure drift in the sweep and implementable in standard-library code on top of the kit's existing hook; the cost overhead and the hook parity of the other two agent products must be measured first
cheap_local_trial: In a scratch copy of the repository: a 4-state JSON state file and a short check in a copy of the guard hook, then a 10-iteration dry loop with 30-second fake training runs, counting out-of-state tool calls with and without the gate

candidate: Confirmation holdout with a read budget (reusable holdout, arXiv 1506.02629)
what: Validation data is split into a search split the loop may use freely and a confirmation split that only harness code reads, a limited number of times, with coarse feedback
problem_here: Dozens of keep-or-revert decisions against one validation set bias the kept score upward; the sealed test set is for the final evaluation only, so nothing protects the intermediate decisions
mechanism: Harness code evaluates kept candidates on the confirmation split, reports pass or fail against a pre-declared threshold (optionally with added noise), counts reads and refuses when the budget is spent
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629 (2015, theory with experiments): adaptive reuse can bias a holdout by about sqrt(k/n); none of the agent-search studies read here reports a hidden test set (arXiv 2603.24647, arXiv 2607.29626, optim-agent README), so the size of the effect in agent loops is unmeasured
maturity: Mature statistical result from 2015, outside the freshness window but not time-sensitive; no agent-loop implementation found
cost: Less validation data for the search; a second evaluation per kept change; threshold and budget must be set before the loop starts
simpler_alternative: Report the sealed-test result once at the end and label every in-loop score as optimistic
reason: Standard-library answer to the main validity risk of an unattended loop; needs a trial because the cost in data and the right read budget depend on the task
cheap_local_trial: On a small classifier with label noise, run 50 random keep-or-revert steps against one validation split and compare the kept score with a fresh split; about 15 minutes on the GPU
